readme:
# Shine.com Jobs Scraper: Job Listings from India

Get job listings from [Shine.com](https://www.shine.com/), a large Indian job board, as clean dataset rows. Search by keyword and city. Each row has the title, company, locations, salary range, required experience, skills, posting date and the job link. Turn on job page details to add the full description, closing date, industry, functional area and application count.

## What you can do with it

- Build a list of companies and recruiters that hire for a skill or role in an Indian city, for sales, staffing or market research.
- Track the Indian job market over time: run it on a schedule and watch new postings, salary ranges and skills in demand.
- Feed a job board, alert service or analytics dashboard with current Indian jobs.
- Compare demand for skills and salary ranges across cities.

## What you get

One dataset row per job. Jobs found by several searches are returned once, and duplicates are removed before anything is charged, so the number of rows is the number of results you pay for. Fields that a job does not have are `null`. Arrays are always arrays (`[]` when empty).

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | Shine job id, the last part of the job URL. Dedup key |
| `title` | Job title |
| `company_name`, `company_id`, `company_logo` | Employer or recruiting agency, its Shine id and logo (when the listing has one) |
| `location`, `locations` | All job locations as text and as a list |
| `location_states`, `country`, `reporting_location` | City and state of each location, ISO country code, reporting location. Need job page details |
| `skills`, `badges` | Skills of the job, listing badges such as `activelyHiring` and `earlyApplicant` |
| `instant_apply`, `direct_apply` | Whether candidates can apply on Shine in one step |
| `salary_label` | Salary text as shown on Shine, for example `5 - 10 Lakh/Yr` or `Not Disclosed` |
| `salary_min`, `salary_max`, `salary_currency`, `salary_period`, `salary_hidden` | The salary range in rupees (`INR`) per `year` or `month`, only when the listing states one. `salary_hidden` is `true` for `Not Disclosed`. Nothing is estimated |
| `experience_label`, `experience_min_years`, `experience_max_years` | Required experience as shown (`2 to 7 Yrs`) and as numbers |
| `experience_required_months` | Experience from the job posting data. Needs job page details |
| `employment_type`, `industry`, `functional_areas` | Employment type (for example `FULL_TIME`), industry and department. Need job page details |
| `vacancies` | Number of open positions when the page states it. Needs job page details |
| `application_count`, `work_mode_code` | Applications Shine shows for the job and the numeric work mode code the site publishes. Need job page details |
| `posted_at`, `valid_through` | Posting time and closing time, ISO 8601 with the `+05:30` offset (India time). `valid_through` needs job page details |
| `description`, `description_text` | Full description as published and as plain text. Need job page details |
| `job_url`, `apply_url` | Job page on Shine. Applications run on that page, so `apply_url` equals `job_url` |
| `details_fetched` | `true` when the job page was read for the row |
| `search_query`, `search_location`, `source`, `scraped_at` | Keyword and city filter that found the job, site host, scrape time (UTC) |

Fields marked "Need job page details" are `null` or empty when `includeDetails` is off.

## Input

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | string[] | Keywords or job titles, one search each (default `python`) |
| `location` | string | City, for example `bangalore`. Combined with every keyword. Empty = all of India |
| `includeDetails` | boolean | Read each job page for the description and more (default `false`, one extra request per job) |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | integer | Cap per keyword (default 50, maximum 1000) |
| `maxResults` | integer | Total cap across all keywords (0 = no limit) |

Shine shows 20 jobs per page. All input fields are optional; an empty input runs the sample below.

### Example input

```json
{"searchQueries": ["python"], "maxResults": 20}
```

### Example: city search with details

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["data analyst", "business analyst"],
  "location": "bangalore",
  "includeDetails": true,
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 100,
  "maxResults": 150
}
```

## Sample output

```json
{
  "id": "19894375",
  "title": "Data Analyst",
  "company_name": "USHTA TE CONSULTANCY SERVICES LLP",
  "company_id": 741434,
  "company_logo": null,
  "location": "Bangalore, Indore",
  "locations": ["Bangalore", "Indore"],
  "location_states": [
    {"city": "Bangalore", "state": "Karnataka"},
    {"city": "Indore", "state": "Madhya Pradesh"}
  ],
  "country": "IN",
  "reporting_location": "Mumbai",
  "skills": ["gap analysis", "csv"],
  "badges": ["activelyHiring"],
  "instant_apply": true,
  "direct_apply": true,
  "salary_label": "Not Disclosed",
  "salary_min": null,
  "salary_max": null,
  "salary_currency": null,
  "salary_period": null,
  "salary_hidden": true,
  "experience_label": "2 to 7 Yrs",
  "experience_min_years": 2,
  "experience_max_years": 7,
  "experience_required_months": 24,
  "employment_type": "FULL_TIME",
  "industry": "Retail",
  "functional_areas": ["Supply Chain / Logistics"],
  "vacancies": null,
  "application_count": 274,
  "work_mode_code": 0,
  "posted_at": "2026-10-22T13:54:31+05:30",
  "valid_through": "2026-11-06T13:54:29+05:30",
  "description": "We are seeking a skilled Data Analyst to join our team in Karnataka or Madhya Pradesh. ...",
  "description_text": "We are seeking a skilled Data Analyst to join our team in Karnataka or Madhya Pradesh. ...",
  "job_url": "https://www.shine.com/jobs/data-analyst/ushta-te-consultancy-services-llp/19894375",
  "apply_url": "https://www.shine.com/jobs/data-analyst/ushta-te-consultancy-services-llp/19894375",
  "details_fetched": true,
  "search_query": "data analyst",
  "search_location": "bangalore",
  "source": "www.shine.com",
  "scraped_at": "2026-11-06T08:00:00Z"
}
```

The sample is a row with job page details, with the description shortened.

You are responsible for using the data lawfully, including data-protection laws and the rules for marketing and outreach.

## Pricing (Pay-per-event)

Price: $0.001 start fee per run, then $0.0015 per job result ($1.50 per 1,000 jobs).

The start fee is charged once per run and the result fee once per job row. Duplicates are never charged. Set a maximum total charge on the run to stop at a budget: the run ends cleanly when it is reached, and the status message says how many jobs were delivered. The pricing box on the actor page always shows the current rates.

## FAQ

**Why does a search return fewer jobs than the site counts?**
Shine shows 20 jobs per page and the run stops at the end of the results, at `maxResultsPerQuery`, or at `maxResults`. A job that appears on two pages or in two searches is returned once.

**Why is the salary empty?**
Many employers do not disclose it. Then `salary_label` is `Not Disclosed`, `salary_hidden` is `true` and the amounts are `null`. The actor never estimates a salary.

**Why do some rows have no description?**
The description comes from the job page. Turn `includeDetails` on. If a single job page cannot be read (for example the job was removed), the row is still delivered with the search fields and `details_fetched` is `false`.

**What happens when nothing matches?**
The run finishes with the status `0 jobs found for <keywords>.` and charges only the start fee. If Shine blocks every request, the run fails with a clear status instead of reporting an empty result.

## Limits

- Jobs in India only, as listed on Shine.com.
- Up to 1000 jobs per keyword. Use narrower searches (city, keyword) for more.
- Posting times are India time (`+05:30`).
- Shine does not publish recruiter contact data on public pages, so none is returned.

## Support

- **Questions or issues?** Email contact@nanoscrape.com or open a ticket in the Issues tab on the actor page.
- **Need a scraper for a job board we do not cover yet?** Email contact@nanoscrape.com with the target site and your rough usage volume.
